wiki-iran.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Iran, a country of some 90 million people between the Caspian and the Gulf. The count rises when Iran enters the news somewhere far from it, which makes it a rough gauge of how widely a story has travelled.
wiki-iran.recent: Austria revoked a visa it had already granted Mohammad Eslami, barring Iran's nuclear chief from the IAEA meeting in Vienna even as Iran's mission took a General Committee seat. A US government report on the six-month war disclosed 18 American dead, dozens of aircraft lost and no decision on whether damaged Gulf bases will be rebuilt.

brent.standing: The price of a barrel of light, sweet crude from the North Sea, and the grade against which roughly two-thirds of the world's traded oil is priced. Refiners from Rotterdam to Singapore settle against it, and fuel prices follow.
brent.recent: Houthi forces took Yemen's Red Sea coast and the strait beside it, cutting the tanker route that feeds Europe and Asia. Drones then shut the East-West pipeline at Yanbu, the only line that lets Saudi barrels skip Hormuz, leaving export stocks days from empty. Washington added a bill tariffing buyers of Russian oil at 100%.

wti.standing: The price of a barrel of West Texas Intermediate, the light sweet crude delivered at Cushing, Oklahoma that sets the dollar benchmark for North American oil. US refiners, shale producers and drivers all price off it.
wti.recent: US strikes on three Iranian crude tankers and explosions on Kharg Island, Iran's main export terminal, pulled barrels out of the Gulf, and Houthi fighters then took Yemen's port of Mocha and pushed toward the Red Sea lane. Argus puts the loss of exports at 7 million barrels a day. The repricing reached US consumer prices, which rose 0.4% in August.

natgas-hh.standing: The US benchmark price for natural gas, settled at a pipeline junction in Erath, Louisiana, where major interstate lines meet. Almost every American gas contract prices off it, and it sets what power generators and industrial users pay.
natgas-hh.recent: The Gulf war that drove European gas above €75 per megawatt-hour and October futures to $1,004 per 1,000 cubic meters has barely touched the US price, because Henry Hub trades a domestic pipeline market rather than the seaborne one. The stranded Qatari cargoes pushed China and India to coal and oil instead, so the substitution landed in Asia, not on American gas.

wheat.standing: The global benchmark price for a tonne of milling wheat, tracked by the IMF from major export quotations. It sets what importing governments pay to keep bread subsidised, and it feeds through to the cost of flour, feed grain and livestock everywhere.
wheat.recent: The UN food agency's index rose for a third month to 133.3 points, with cereals among the drivers, and it named conflict and extreme weather as the causes. Forecasters warned of an El Nino that could be the strongest in decades and run well into 2027, threatening the harvests that follow.

rice.standing: The IMF's benchmark price for milled white rice traded out of Thailand, the reference most Asian and West African import contracts are written against. Rice feeds more people daily than any other grain, so its price lands on household food bills first.
rice.recent: Nigeria's consumer price index reached 146.3 points last month, and in Ekiti state ofada growers including Abu Ibrahim quit the crop after a dry spell and unpredictable rain rotted two harvests with no insurance behind them. The UN food agency's index rose a third month to 133.3 points on conflict and extreme weather.

copper.standing: The world price of a tonne of refined copper, the metal that carries electricity. Grids, motors, transformers and building wire are all claims on it, so its price is the running cost of electrification.
copper.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's reporting explains the price. What copper appeared in was biology and sabotage: Texas A&M researchers working on how immune cells use copper against bacteria in College Station, and the explosives found on power lines in Saxony, which threatened German grid hardware rather than any supply of the metal.

us-10y.standing: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for ten years, set by auction and trading in the deepest bond market in the world. It is the reference price for long-dated dollar debt, so mortgages, corporate loans and sovereign borrowing everywhere are quoted off it.
us-10y.recent: The long-end selloff is term premium rather than policy: investors are demanding more to hold duration while the Fed is being pushed toward a hike, a call Goldman Sachs reversed after Houthi forces took Yemen's port of Mocha and crude ran to $105. The repricing reaches borrowers far from Washington — Nigeria's index reclassification is expected to draw $17.5 billion at 200 basis points more.

sp500.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of 500 large companies listed in the United States, chosen by a committee rather than by size alone. It is the default benchmark for American equity, and most retirement money tracks it.
sp500.recent: Chip stocks led a global sell-off after a warning about AI capital spending came from an investor already on the cap table, and the drop ran to 8% in semiconductors — the heaviest weights in the index. Bond yields at multi-decade highs and an August inflation increase driven by petrol costs pushed against any recovery.

nasdaq100.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange in New York. Software, chipmakers and consumer-device firms dominate it, so it moves as a proxy for the technology trade itself.
nasdaq100.recent: The drop came from the chip complex, which fell 8% in a global sell-off on doubts about how much AI capacity buyers will actually pay for — the same week Anthropic was reported to be choosing Nasdaq for a listing that could raise $100 billion at a $2 trillion valuation. Apple shipped a rebuilt Siri onto a billion devices two days earlier.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average pump price American drivers pay for a gallon of regular gasoline, surveyed weekly across the country. It tracks crude and refining margins with a lag, and it is the cost-of-living number US households see most often.
us-gas-retail.recent: The Iran war pushed Brent near $109.50 a barrel, and refined products moved faster than crude: diesel set a record at $5.85 a gallon before topping $6.06, and petrol passed 2012's record at $4.03. Houthi missiles burned Aramco's Red Sea refinery at Jizan, and Trump pressed Zelenskyy to stop striking Russian refineries — refining capacity, not barrels, is the binding constraint.

natgas-ttf.standing: The Dutch Title Transfer Facility price, the benchmark for gas delivered into northwest Europe's pipeline grid and the reference most European industrial and heating contracts settle against. Since the continent turned to seaborne LNG it clears against Asian buyers.
natgas-ttf.recent: October futures touched $1,004 per 1,000 cubic meters in Amsterdam, a level last paid in December 2022, after a rush to fill storage collided with an LNG shortage. Qatari cargoes have been held up by the Gulf war, and China and India answered the price by burning coal and oil instead — while Bangladesh committed to two new import terminals by 2030.

vix.standing: A gauge of how much movement options traders are paying to hedge in the S&P 500 over the coming month. It rises when big investors bid up protection, so it reads as the price of insurance rather than a forecast.

fx-pkr.standing: The rupee's price against the US dollar. Pakistan imports nearly all its oil and much of its food, so the rate sets the domestic cost of fuel and grain, and the burden of the country's dollar-denominated debt.
fx-pkr.recent: The State Bank held its policy rate steady in Karachi with Brent near $110 a barrel, keeping the import bill heavy. Islamabad raised diesel Rs6.10 to Rs409.42 a litre while leaving Rs114 a litre in tax on petrol, then funded a motorcycle fuel subsidy from that same levy rather than from reserves.

fx-ngn.standing: The exchange rate of Nigeria's naira against the US dollar. Nigeria earns its foreign currency mainly from crude oil sales, so the rate sets the price of nearly everything imported into Africa's largest consumer market.
fx-ngn.recent: Washington lifted a 12-year shipping restriction on Nigerian ports, and index providers moved to reclassify Nigerian bonds, a change expected to draw $17.5 billion of foreign money into naira-denominated debt. Consumer prices are still climbing, reaching 146.3 points last month, so the currency's steadiness is not disinflation reaching the street.

fx-egp.standing: The price of one US dollar in Egyptian pounds. Egypt imports most of its wheat and fuel, so the rate sets the cost of bread and electricity, and it governs how far remittances from Gulf workers stretch at home.
fx-egp.recent: Cairo hosted Xi Jinping's first state visit in a decade, where he pressed Middle East governments to build a security order without outside bases, and Putin talked up widening Russian trade with Egypt — both courting a government that has been rationing hard currency. At home the state moved the subsidized fertilizer system away from cooperatives in five governorates.

fx-try.standing: The value of Turkey's currency against the US dollar, quoted as lira per dollar, so a rising number means a weakening lira. Turkey imports most of its energy in dollars, and the rate feeds straight into domestic inflation.
fx-try.recent: Ankara revised its medium-term growth forecast downward, and the US Treasury sanctioned Golden Global Bank in Istanbul over Iran-related dealings, a designation the bank threatened to fight in court. Both land on a currency whose external financing depends on foreign banks' willingness to keep clearing Turkish trade.

fx-bdt.standing: The price of one US dollar in Bangladeshi taka, the managed rate Bangladesh Bank steers within a narrow band. The country imports its fuel, industrial inputs and much of its food, so the rate sets the cost of nearly everything that lands at Chittagong.
fx-bdt.recent: Dhaka spent the month committing to more dollar-denominated energy imports rather than fewer: two new LNG terminals due by 2030, and a $1 billion Islamic Development Bank facility for domestic refining capacity that only pays off years out. A ministerial row with Delhi over the terms of the relationship added friction to the trade Bangladesh runs closest to home.

fx-idr.standing: The exchange rate for Indonesia's currency against the US dollar, quoted as rupiah per dollar, so a rising number means a weaker rupiah. Indonesia funds a large share of its debt abroad, and importers of fuel and food pay this rate first.

fx-lbp.standing: The exchange rate of Lebanon's currency against the US dollar. After the 2019 banking collapse wiped out most of its value, the rate has been held near a fixed level by the central bank, and it sets the price of nearly everything imported into the country.
fx-lbp.recent: The pound held flat through a fortnight of escalation in the south: Israeli strikes destroyed Ghandour Hospital in Nabatieh al-Fawqa on Sep 6, killing seven, and a demolition of Hezbollah's Ali al-Taher tunnel network on Sep 11 registered as a tremor. A Lebanese official said talks with Israel were unlikely the following week. None of it reached the rate, which the central bank pins.

fx-cny.standing: China's currency measured against the dollar, quoted as yuan per dollar, so a lower number means a stronger yuan. The People's Bank of China fixes a daily reference rate and allows trading only within a band around it, making this a managed rate.
fx-cny.recent: China led the fortnight's news on other ground entirely: Beijing turned export controls on individuals rather than goods, Xi pitched an AI "open ecosystem" to BRICS partners in New Delhi, and installed solar capacity passed coal. None of it touches the exchange rate, and nothing in the period's reporting accounts for where the currency sits.

fx-inr.standing: The number of rupees it takes to buy one US dollar, set in Mumbai's onshore market under a Reserve Bank of India that intervenes to smooth swings. India imports most of its crude, so the rate feeds straight into fuel and fertiliser costs.
fx-inr.recent: The rupee's weakest reading of the month landed as the US House advanced a sanctions bill, by three votes, that would let the president impose 100% tariffs on buyers of Russian oil — India being the buyer it was written for. Modi spent the fortnight at a BRICS summit in New Delhi discussing linked local-currency payment rails with the same partners.

fx-brl.standing: The price of one US dollar in Brazilian reais, the floating currency of Latin America's largest economy. It is one of the most heavily traded emerging-market currencies, and it swings on commodity export earnings, domestic politics and the gap between Brazilian and US interest rates.
fx-brl.recent: Political risk, not trade, dominated the fortnight: police opened a probe into Flávio Bolsonaro over film financing as the election tightened, the Banco Master scandal widened through Brasília, and a new poll showed the president's lead evaporating. Washington's designation of the PCC as a terror organisation added a second front to the campaign.

fx-mxn.standing: The exchange rate of Mexico's peso against the US dollar, one of the most heavily traded emerging-market currencies and the one that clears the largest cross-border manufacturing relationship in the world. Tariff and migration policy move it first.

fx-eur.standing: The price of one euro against the US dollar, quoted here as euros per dollar. It is the world's second most-held reserve currency and the exchange rate through which the eurozone's trade, borrowing and energy bills are settled.

fx-jpy.standing: The exchange rate between Japan's yen and the US dollar, quoted as yen per dollar, so a rising number means a weaker yen. It is the world's most traded pair after the euro, and the funding leg of carry trades that reach far beyond Japan.
fx-jpy.recent: Tokyo moved from talk to instruments: officials weighed steering the currency through pension money rather than outright intervention, reviving the 2014 playbook. The Fed backdrop cut the other way, with a Waller-driven dollar slide and an oil shock pushing hike odds to two-in-three, before SoftBank's 13% Monday drop pulled Tokyo risk appetite back.

fx-rub.standing: The exchange rate of Russia's currency against the US dollar, quoted as rubles per dollar. Capital controls and oil export receipts set its level, and a weaker ruble flatters the Kremlin's budget by inflating the domestic value of energy sales.
fx-rub.recent: The US House advanced a bill by three votes that would let Trump impose 100% tariffs on buyers of Russian oil, with India the named target; a Senate version had already passed. Trump separately ordered a halt to Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries, and European states kept detaining aging tankers from the shadow fleet Putin warned them over.

fx-zar.standing: The value of one US dollar in South African rand, the most heavily traded currency in Africa and a standing proxy for emerging-market risk. It reflects mining export receipts, domestic politics and the dollar rate cycle at once.
fx-zar.recent: Washington imposed visa restrictions on foreign nationals resident in South Africa, an order Rubio announced without naming individuals, and it lands on a relationship already strained by US objections to Pretoria's land-reform law and its ICJ genocide case against Israel. A §212(a)(3)(C) curb needs no evidence or hearing, which makes further pressure cheap to apply.

btc.standing: The price of one bitcoin, the first and largest cryptocurrency, quoted against the dollar across exchanges. It trades continuously, has no issuer or cash flows behind it, and is the reference asset the rest of the crypto market prices off.
btc.recent: The Digital Asset Market Clarity Act died on a procedural vote in the Senate, ending the industry's push to move oversight from the SEC to the CFTC and leaving regulation to enforcement instead; Coinbase fell nearly 9 percent alongside bitcoin. Earlier, a bug drained roughly 4,000 bitcoin from Liquid Network's reserve.

eth.standing: The native token of the Ethereum network, the largest smart-contract platform, where it pays the fees that execute code and settle transactions. Most stablecoins and tokenised assets live on rails it secures, so demand for that block space sets its bid.

paxg.standing: A token redeemable for one fine troy ounce of London Good Delivery gold held in vaults, so it tracks the spot bullion price while trading around the clock on crypto exchanges. It carries custody risk a bar in hand does not.
paxg.recent: A US payroll surge pushed traders toward a September rate hike, and gold sells off when the return on holding cash rises. Higher oil kept those bets alive into the week. Beneath the price, custody moved: the Dutch central bank shifted $11.6bn of gold out of New York to London, which the Financial Conduct Authority says handles 70% of global trading.

wiki-artificial-intelligence.standing: A Wikipedia article on machines that perform tasks associated with human reasoning — learning, perception, language, decision-making. Its readership is one of the plainest measures of how far the subject has travelled beyond the people who build it.
wiki-artificial-intelligence.recent: Two AI lab founders called publicly for a slowdown, Amodei warning that a "swarm" could seize the internet, and within a day chip stocks led an 8% global sell-off and SoftBank fell 13% in Tokyo. Trump dismissed the safety warnings as a "sick conspiracy" and declined guardrails; Gartner put 86% of CIOs saying risk outpaces value.

wiki-russia.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Russia, the largest country on earth by land area and a permanent member of the UN Security Council. Reader traffic to a country's page tends to follow the days it drives world news.
wiki-russia.recent: The fortnight's news from Russia ran on several tracks at once. A US bill advanced through Congress that would let Trump impose 100% tariffs on buyers of Russian oil, aimed squarely at India, while Trump separately told Kyiv to stop striking Russian refineries as US diesel passed $6.06 a gallon.

wiki-pakistan.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Pakistan, a country of some 250 million people wedged between Afghanistan, Iran, India and China. The count rises when the country enters a story big enough to send strangers looking it up.
wiki-pakistan.recent: Islamabad spent the fortnight taxing fuel and then refunding it: petrol carries a levy of 114 rupees a litre, diesel rose Rs6.10 to Rs409.42, a march set off from Gujranwala, and Shehbaz Sharif answered with a motorcycle subsidy funded by the same levy. Abroad, Iran's minister routed a Houthi-Saudi approach through Islamabad.

wiki-china.standing: The daily count of people opening the English Wikipedia article on China. It rises when something makes a general audience look the country up rather than read a specific story, so it tracks broad curiosity rather than news volume.
wiki-china.recent: Beijing spent the fortnight asserting control over what leaves the country: exit bans on technologists carrying chip knowledge, and Chang'e 7, the probe meant to find lunar ice, slipped with no new date given. Xi used Modi's BRICS summit to pitch an AI "open ecosystem" as an alternative stack, while Hangzhou firms cut humanoid robots to $13,500 and robot dogs to $4,000.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: The sea lane between Iran and Oman linking the Gulf to the Arabian Sea, roughly 33 km wide at its narrowest. Around a fifth of the world's oil and a large share of its liquefied natural gas leaves through it, with no full-capacity alternative route.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: Drones shut Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, the one export line that skips the strait, while a projectile killed a sailor off Qeshm Island and Tehran floated transit fees. Muscat's talks on the channel were shelved after Bahrain stayed away, and China and India burned coal and oil in place of gas that did not arrive.

wiki-india.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on India, a country of over a billion people whose entry is one of the encyclopedia's most-read national pages. Its traffic climbs when Delhi is at the centre of a global story.
wiki-india.recent: New Delhi hosted the BRICS summit, where Modi held 15 bilateral meetings in three days and Xi shared the stage as the war involving Iran deepened; the final declaration kept the words on a right of return, and India offered the bloc its UPI payments network, which clears over 250 billion transfers a year. Washington then moved a bill letting Trump tariff buyers of Russian oil at 100%.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: Traffic thinned as the war reached the shipping itself: a projectile struck a tanker off Qeshm Island and killed a sailor, and Iraqi investigators traced a launch platform on Tayeb Island. Drones from Iraq then shut the Saudi East-West line, the one pipeline that bypasses the strait, and Yanbu export stocks were days from running out.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: Houthi fighters took the Red Sea coast and now hold Perim Island beside the lane itself, having seized the coffee port of Mokha, 75 kilometers up the coast, days earlier. Some 46,000 people fled the coastline as the front moved, and Brent crude reached $109.50 a barrel. Saudi jets answered with 54 sorties across five provinces in a day.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.
cp:suez.recent: Houthi fighters took Mocha and the rest of Yemen's Red Sea coast, then seized Perim Island in the Bab al-Mandab, the southern gate every northbound ship must pass before reaching Egypt. Some 46,000 people fled the coast, Brent topped $108 a barrel, and carriers routing away from the strait take Suez traffic with them.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.
cp:malacca.recent: Iran's Strait Authority moved against tanker insurers this week, and a projectile hit a tanker near Hormuz — the war at the far end of the route decides what reaches this one. With Qatari cargoes stalled, China and India cut LNG imports to multi-year lows and burned coal to cover the gap.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.
cp:taiwan.recent: Traffic held near its own baseline while the pressure on the strait moved off the water and into the supply chain around it. Beijing began barring semiconductor staff from leaving the country, an export control applied to people rather than goods, and Lithuania's ultrafast lasers surfaced as an input Taiwan's fabs cannot easily replace.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.
cp:panama.recent: The canal authority moved to hold daily transits at 29 rather than 32 as water rationing tightened, the operator's response to an El Nino the UN has warned may be the strongest in decades and which forecasters already have driving a record Amazon drought. Slot cuts are the canal's only lever once the watershed runs short.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: Two ships collided off Silivri on 2 September, sinking a Turkish cargo vessel and leaving ten crew missing — the kind of incident that slows the queue at the strait's approaches, where traffic waits rather than transits. Turkey controls passage under Montreux but not the congestion outside it. Ankara cut its medium-term growth forecast on 11 September.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.
cp:gibraltar.recent: The fortnight's news from the strait's two shores was about people rather than cargo: Spain's government faced protests over its handling of a migrant surge into Ceuta and questioned Morocco's border control, and Morocco deported over 4,000 people from Tangier in 20 days. None of that reaches shipping.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.
cp:dover.recent: Masked protesters shut Dover, Britain's busiest ferry port, on 5 September, halting cross-Channel freight; two days later crowds at Portsmouth blocked buses carrying 140 asylum seekers who had crossed from Normandy. The disruption fell on the ferry and ro-ro trade rather than the through-traffic in the separation lanes.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: Traffic on the detour has thinned even as the Gulf grew more dangerous, because the disruption moved to the other end of the voyage: a projectile hit a tanker near Hormuz, three more turned back without a shot fired, and Iran's Strait Authority updated a non-compliant vessel list aimed at insurers. Cargo that never loads never rounds Africa.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.
cp:kerch.recent: Traffic has stopped entirely. European states have been detaining aging tankers from Russia's shadow fleet, and Putin warned that seizures would not go unanswered; the US House advanced a bill letting the president impose 100% tariffs on buyers of Russian oil, passing by three votes. Odesa was struck Saturday, wounding 37.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The main index of the Saudi Exchange in Riyadh, the Arab world's largest market by value, weighted heavily toward Aramco. It trades Sunday to Thursday, so it opens the global week before Tokyo.
mkt:tadawul.recent: Drones launched from Iraq's Maysan province shut the East-West pipeline, the only line that moves Saudi crude to the Red Sea without passing Hormuz, and traders at Yanbu put export stocks days from exhaustion. Houthi forces then seized Mocha and islands near Bab al-Mandeb, and missiles reached four Saudi cities and King Khalid Air Base.

mkt:bist.standing: The 100 largest companies by weight on Borsa İstanbul, Türkiye's only stock exchange. Priced in lira, so its index level carries the country's inflation as much as its earnings — read the direction, not the number.
mkt:bist.recent: Ankara revised its medium-term growth forecast downward, writing regional war into the official numbers banks and industrials are valued against. The US Treasury then sanctioned Golden Global Bank over Iran-linked dealings, and the lender threatened legal action — a reminder that Turkish financial institutions remain exposed to Washington's enforcement reach.

mkt:dfm.standing: The benchmark index of the Dubai Financial Market, the emirate's stock exchange, tracking its listed shares. It is the Gulf's main listing venue for property and banking, and trades Monday to Friday rather than Riyadh's Sunday-to-Thursday week.
mkt:dfm.recent: Dubai is absorbing the costs of the Iran war it sits beside: the Hormuz closure pushed Emirates-Oman land trade up 175% as cargo found overland routes, US forces struck three Iranian tankers, and Algeria expelled the Emirati envoy over the UAE's regional role. Against that, oil exports fell 7 million barrels daily without Brent holding above 100.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The 30 largest companies listed on Bursa Malaysia in Kuala Lumpur, weighted by free-float market value. It is the world's largest market for Islamic finance instruments, and the centre of the global sukuk trade.

mkt:idx.standing: The benchmark index of the Indonesia Stock Exchange in Jakarta, tracking every listed company on the market. It belongs to the world's largest Muslim-majority country and leans heavily on commodity producers and banks.

mkt:tse.standing: The 225 large Japanese companies tracked by a price-weighted average on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, Asia's largest market and the first major one to price each trading day.
mkt:tse.recent: SoftBank shares slumped 13% on Monday as markets repriced how fast AI spending will actually arrive, dragging the index's heaviest constituents with it. The yen has been the other pressure: US Treasury Secretary Bessent urged Japan to raise rates, and Tokyo has weighed steering the currency through pension money rather than intervention.

mkt:hkex.standing: The Hang Seng Index tracks the largest and most heavily traded companies listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. It is where mainland Chinese firms meet foreign capital, and the clearest daily read on sentiment toward China.
mkt:hkex.recent: Beijing extended export control to people, barring tech staff from leaving the country, and a Hong Kong court jailed vigil organizers for seven years — both reach the listings foreign money buys here. In the same fortnight Unitree's cost-cutting put a walking robot at $13,500 and a quadruped at $4,000, while tech stocks tumbled as AI fears went mainstream.

mkt:sse.standing: Mainland China's main board, in Shanghai, tracking every A- and B-share listed there — state banks, insurers and industrial groups by weight. Largely closed to foreign investors, so it follows domestic policy more than global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: Beijing widened its tech controls from goods to people, barring staff at sensitive firms from leaving the country — a policy reach that lands directly on the listed technology names. The AI trade that carried the board also cooled as the selloff in tech shares spread, and Chang'e 7 slipped with no new date given.

mkt:krx.standing: South Korea's benchmark index, tracking every common stock listed on the main board of the Korea Exchange in Seoul. Samsung and SK Hynix dominate it, which makes it a proxy for the global semiconductor cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: Seoul spent the window arguing about warships: the government denied preparing a Strait of Hormuz deployment even as 601 civic groups marched against one, in a country whose industry runs on crude that transits the strait. North Korea fired missiles 250 kilometers from Wonsan after US-South Korea drills.

mkt:bse.standing: The 30-company benchmark of the Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai, Asia's oldest exchange, founded in 1875, and the reference index for Indian equities.
mkt:bse.recent: A sanctions bill that cleared the Senate and then passed the House by three votes lets Washington impose a 100% tariff on buyers of Russian oil — and India is the buyer it was drafted around, with the levy falling on the importer rather than the seller. Domestic policy added a second drag: the Unified Payments Interface, free since launch, now charges fees above Rs 2,000.

mkt:sgx.standing: The 30 largest companies listed in Singapore, the city-state's main market. Banks and regional property groups dominate it, so it tracks credit conditions across Southeast Asia rather than Singapore's own economy alone.
mkt:sgx.recent: Singapore kept widening what its market is allowed to clear: SGX opened bitcoin and ether perpetual futures to US institutions after the Commodity Futures Trading Commission signed off, and Circle paid $400 million for Tazapay's payment licenses in more than 100 markets. China's August exports rose 25% to $401 billion, feeding the regional trade the index's banks finance.

mkt:twse.standing: Taiwan's headline index, tracking every common share listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange in Taipei by market value. TSMC alone is roughly a third of the index, which makes this the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: The fortnight's Taiwan news ran to security rather than earnings: Taipei accused China of espionage on the floor of the Pacific forum, prosecutors pursued engineers recruited into undeclared Chinese chip labs, and Lithuania's femtosecond laser makers turned out to sit inside the toolchain the fabs depend on. None of it accounts for the index's path.

mkt:set.standing: The main board index of the Stock Exchange of Thailand in Bangkok, weighted by market value across the listed companies on it. Banks, energy and tourism-exposed firms carry it, so it moves with visitor numbers and fuel costs.
mkt:set.recent: Thai artillery hit the Preah Vihear temple complex on the Cambodian border, and UNESCO has now documented the damage while Bangkok answers that Cambodia stationed troops there first — a live border war on the frontier of a market that depends on visitors. Bangkok's semiconductor plan also runs through Washington, which licenses the fabrication equipment.

mkt:pse.standing: The main index of the Philippine Stock Exchange in Manila, tracking 30 of the country's largest and most heavily traded listed companies. It is a small, domestically-driven market where remittance flows move the index.
mkt:pse.recent: Manila's political class spent the fortnight in court: an anti-graft court ordered the arrest of Marcos's own cousin Romualdez over flood-control kickbacks, and Vice President Sara Duterte posted bail on charges of threatening the president. A ferry fire off Coron left 87 unaccounted for.

mkt:asx.standing: The 200 largest listed companies on the Australian Securities Exchange, weighted by float-adjusted market value. Mining and banking dominate it, so it is often the first major market to react to Chinese demand data.
mkt:asx.recent: Miners and energy stocks led the slide from early September, and the index hit a six-week low on Sep 8 before rate fears drove another slump. Canberra is weighing a subsidy to keep an aluminium smelter open rather than let it close, and One Nation's pledge to cut 750,000 temporary migrants over three years targets the population growth the banks lend into.

mkt:jse.standing: The FTSE/JSE All Share Index tracks almost every company listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange in South Africa, weighted by tradable shares. It is Africa's largest exchange by far, and the continent's only one with a usable public daily series.
mkt:jse.recent: Pretoria absorbed two shocks in the window: statisticians reported a quarter of economic contraction, and Washington imposed visa curbs on foreign nationals resident in South Africa, a consular instrument that needs no hearing and no published finding. The pressure campaign runs to the land-reform law, racial-redress policy and the ICJ genocide case against Israel.

mkt:b3.standing: The Ibovespa is the main index of B3, the São Paulo exchange and Latin America's largest. It weights its constituents by traded volume, so iron ore, oil and bank shares dominate, and Brazilian interest rates move it.
mkt:b3.recent: Brazil's election campaign supplied the window's politics: police opened a probe into Flávio Bolsonaro over film financing in Brasília, Washington listed the PCC as a terrorist organisation, and a poll showed the president's lead evaporating. Brasília also moved to align its carbon markets with international pricing.

mkt:bmv.standing: The Índice de Precios y Cotizaciones, the main index of the Bolsa Mexicana de Valores in Mexico City, tracking the most traded shares on Mexico's largest exchange. It is tightly coupled to US demand and to the peso.

mkt:byma.standing: The benchmark index of the Buenos Aires exchange, tracking Argentina's most heavily traded listed companies. Priced in a currency that has lost most of its value repeatedly, so the index rises even in bad years — direction over a day means something; the level does not.
mkt:byma.recent: Milei reopened the Falklands claim, sanctioning 45 firms tied to UK-linked oil drilling around the islands, and Trump put the long-standing US position on the dispute under review. Washington then approved a $103m Black Hawk sale to Buenos Aires. Monthly inflation, meanwhile, fell to a 14-month low.

mkt:tsx.standing: Canada's benchmark index, tracking the largest companies listed in Toronto by float-adjusted market value. Oil and gas producers, miners and the big domestic banks dominate the weighting, so it trades as much on commodities as on Canadian growth.
mkt:tsx.recent: Washington put 50% tariffs on Canadian goods and banned dairy, alcohol and motorcycles outright, then threatened Bombardier by name; Ottawa's $20 billion in counter-tariffs took effect Tuesday. Carney answered by pitching associate EU membership to investors managing $72tn in Toronto — a reorientation of trade built to run north-south.

mkt:nyse.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of 500 large US companies listed in New York, the single most widely tracked equity benchmark in the world. Pension funds and index trackers everywhere hold it, so its close sets the tone other markets open against.
mkt:nyse.recent: The drop came out of Washington rather than the earnings calendar: the House advanced a Russia sanctions bill by three votes that exposes buyers of Russian energy, with India facing a 100% tariff, and a Senate crypto bill collapsed in a fight over which regulator would supervise the industry, taking Bitcoin down 5%.

mkt:lse.standing: The Financial Times Stock Exchange 100, the 100 largest companies by market value listed in London. Most of their revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.

mkt:xetra.standing: The 40 largest listed companies on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange, Germany's main market. Its weight in carmakers, chemicals and industrial machinery makes it Europe's clearest read on export demand.
mkt:xetra.recent: Saxony-Anhalt handed the AfD nearly 44% and the first far-right state win since the war, with about 150,000 people marching across 20 German cities afterwards; the other parties held the firewall, leaving coalition arithmetic unresolved. Deutsche Bank raised its ECB peak call to 2.75% on energy costs feeding second-round inflation.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: The 40 largest listed companies in France, traded on Euronext's Paris market. Luxury goods and energy dominate it, which leaves the index unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: Two of the index's defence and technology anchors shifted footing: the Future Combat Air System with Germany collapsed, leaving the Rafale F5 as France's path, and Mistral closed a €3 billion round, Europe's largest tech funding. France also joined 12 countries sanctioning trade from Israeli settlements.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The blue-chip index of the 25 most traded companies on Euronext Amsterdam, the descendant of the world's oldest stock exchange. A single chip-equipment maker, ASML, carries enough weight to move the whole index on its own.
mkt:euronext-amsterdam.recent: Amsterdam is where Europe prices its gas, and the TTF contract traded there ran to a three-year high above €75 per megawatt-hour before October futures reached $1,004 per 1,000 cubic meters — an energy cost that lands on the industrial names listed in the same city. The Dutch central bank also moved $11.6bn in gold out of New York to London.

mkt:bme.standing: The 35 most liquid companies on the Bolsa de Madrid, Spain's main exchange. Spanish banks with heavy Latin American exposure make this a proxy for both regions.
mkt:bme.recent: Spain's summer was dominated by the Ceuta border rather than by anything priced on the exchange: more than 72,000 people crossed into the enclave in July, Morocco deported over 4,000 more from Tangier in twenty days, and the prime minister publicly questioned Moroccan border control. Parliament then backed Sahrawi citizenship 168 to 31, straining the same relationship. None of it explains the index.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: The 40 largest and most traded companies on the Milan exchange, Italy's main market. Banks and utilities carry it, and it is the market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: Giorgia Meloni passed 1,413 days in office, making hers the longest-serving government in Italian history — the stability premium banks here trade on. Former leaders told CNBC that economic reform now has to follow the milestone, and nothing in the fortnight's news touched the lenders directly.

mkt:six.standing: The Swiss Market Index, the 20 largest and most traded companies on the SIX Swiss Exchange in Zurich. Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry the index, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: The 30 most traded companies on Nasdaq Stockholm, Sweden's main market. Nordic industrials and telecoms dominate it, which makes it a useful early read on European capital spending.
mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.recent: Sweden voted on 13 September in a race close enough that SVT's exit poll gave the opposition 51.3% and the count left the blocs at 176 seats to 173 with 95% in. The Sweden Democrats' entry into government was on the ballot for the first time, and neither side can form a majority without a partner it has spent the campaign ruling out.

mkt:tase.standing: The 125 largest companies by market value on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, Israel's only stock market. Banks, defence contractors and technology firms carry most of its weight, and it trades Sunday to Thursday.

poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the Federal Reserve leaves its policy rate untouched at the coming meeting. Traders buy and sell the outcome, so the price is what people will pay for a hold rather than a survey of forecasters.
poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.recent: The bet on a hold thinned as the case for a hike hardened: Houthi fighters took Yemen's port of Mocha on Sep 10 and oil ran to $105, turning an energy shock into an inflation problem, and Goldman Sachs dropped its no-hike call on Friday. The 10-year Treasury yield reached 5%, its highest since 2007, as the Fed's meeting opened.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: The daily count of people opening the English Wikipedia biography of Donald Trump, the 45th and 47th president of the United States. It is one of the site's most-read political pages, and it rises whenever his decisions reach a new audience.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: The early-September peak fell as US strikes on Iran resumed and eleven people were killed. Since then Trump has tied the war's end to the midterms, halted strikes on refineries at the invaded country's request as US diesel topped $6.06 a gallon, lifted a tariff on Irish whiskey "as a favor" at Doonbeg, and backed Irish unification.

wiki-united-states.standing: The number of times the English Wikipedia article on the United States is opened each day. It is a rough gauge of how much of the world is looking up the country itself rather than any one story about it.
wiki-united-states.recent: The Pentagon disclosed that 18 US troops died fighting Iran, and told the congressional scorekeeper that put war costs above $38 billion that it would not answer its questions. Washington also confirmed it already has weapons in orbit, and the Supreme Court left standing an injunction against new mail-ballot rules.

fed-funds.standing: The overnight interest rate the US Federal Reserve sets for banks lending reserves to each other. It is the anchor price of dollar credit worldwide, and mortgages, corporate borrowing and emerging-market debt costs all reprice off it.
fed-funds.recent: An oil shock has turned the debate from cuts to a hike: Brent near $110 after Houthi forces took Yemen's port of Mocha, and August consumer prices up 0.4%. A payroll surge and Goldman Sachs abandoning its no-hike call pushed the 10-year Treasury yield to 5.02%, its highest since 2007, and the 30-year mortgage to 6.71%.

ecb-rate.standing: The rate the European Central Bank pays commercial banks on funds parked with it overnight, and the lever that sets the floor for borrowing costs across the euro area. Mortgage and business lending rates follow it.
ecb-rate.recent: Deutsche Bank lifted its projected ECB peak to 2.75% on the argument that an energy shock is feeding through to second-round wage and price effects rather than fading. The backdrop is a global repricing of long-dated debt: oil near $105 a barrel and multi-decade highs in bond yields have pushed central banks back toward tightening.

us-unemployment.standing: The share of the American labour force looking for work and unable to find it, published monthly by the Bureau of Labor Statistics. The Federal Reserve weighs it against inflation when setting rates, so markets move on each release.
us-unemployment.recent: The jobs report published on 5 September was solid enough that yields and the dollar rose on it while stocks eased — the reaction of a market reading a labour market too firm to force the Fed's hand. Nothing else in the fortnight's reporting points to a deterioration in hiring.

xag.standing: The spot price of a troy ounce of silver, quoted here through a metal-backed token that settles against vaulted bullion. Silver is both a monetary metal and an industrial input, so it answers to investors and to factories at the same time.
xag.recent: Nothing in the window accounts for the move. What it carries instead is demand: China's installed solar capacity passed coal, Gulf panel imports fell as war disrupted supply chains, and Pakistan moved to mandate batteries in its next 800MW solar and wind auction — solar cells are silver's largest industrial use.

wiki-petroleum.standing: Crude oil and the refined fuels drawn from it — the feedstock behind petrol, diesel, jet fuel, plastics and fertiliser. Its price sets transport and manufacturing costs worldwide, and governments subsidise or tax it to control what households pay.
wiki-petroleum.recent: A US-Iran war reached the oil trade from two directions at once. Houthi forces took Yemen's Red Sea coast and the port of Mocha, and drones flown from Iraq struck the Saudi pipeline built to bypass Hormuz, cutting Yanbu's export stocks to days. US pump prices passed $4.03 a gallon; Pakistan answered its 114-rupee levy with a motorcycle fuel subsidy.

us-cpi.standing: The year-over-year change in the US consumer price index, compiled monthly by the Bureau of Labor Statistics from a basket of household goods, rents and services. It sets the terms of Federal Reserve policy and reprices bonds, wages and benefits worldwide.
us-cpi.recent: August consumer prices rose 0.4% on the month, a reading Washington traced to the war's reach into the index rather than to domestic demand.

portwatch-hormuz-tanker.standing: A daily count of laden tankers passing through the Strait of Hormuz, the sea lane between Iran and Oman. Roughly a fifth of the world's oil leaves the Gulf through it, and there is almost no pipeline capacity that avoids it.
portwatch-hormuz-tanker.recent: Transits collapsed as the US-Iran war reached the shipping itself: a projectile killed a sailor off Qeshm Island, Iran's Strait Authority began listing non-compliant vessels to strip their insurance, and drones shut the East-West pipeline that was the only route around the strait. Gulf states shelved the Muscat talks; Emirates-Oman land trade jumped 175%.

portwatch-bab-container.standing: The daily count of container ships transiting the Bab-el-Mandeb strait between Yemen and Djibouti, the southern gate to the Red Sea and the Suez Canal. Almost all Asia–Europe container trade passes through it or reroutes around Africa.
portwatch-bab-container.recent: Houthi fighters took Mocha and the Red Sea coast in September and now hold Perim Island, in the lane itself, while 46,000 people fled the coast in a week. Saudi jets answered with 54 sorties in a day from Khamis Mushait, and Brent crossed $109 as the war closed on the strait.

portwatch-suez-total.standing: A daily count of vessels passing through Egypt's Suez Canal, the sea link between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea. Roughly a tenth of world seaborne trade runs through it, and every ship that avoids it goes around Africa instead.
portwatch-suez-total.recent: Houthi fighters took Mokha and then Perim Island, putting them astride Bab al-Mandab — the southern gate every Suez-bound ship must pass. Owners stopped sending vessels into a strait held by a party that had already hit four Saudi cities, and drones from Iraq's Maysan province shut the East-West pipeline built to bypass Hormuz, so Brent ran to $109.

portwatch-panama-total.standing: The number of ships passing through the Panama Canal each day, the lock-and-lake shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. The locks run on rainwater held in Gatún Lake, so a dry year rations the sailings container and grain lines depend on.
portwatch-panama-total.recent: The canal authority is weighing further cuts to daily slots as El Niño draws down the lake that feeds the locks, with its new chief signalling a drop toward 29. The UN puts the odds the event persists into February near 100% and forecasters expect it to run well into 2027, so the rationing is being set against a dry season that has not yet arrived.

portwatch-malacca-total.standing: The count of ships passing each day through the narrow channel between Sumatra and the Malay Peninsula, the shortest sea route from the Indian Ocean to East Asia. Most of China's and Japan's imported oil crosses it.
portwatch-malacca-total.recent: Traffic through the strait is carrying the diversions from two crises further west. Houthi forces took control of Yemen's Red Sea coast, and a projectile that killed a sailor off Qeshm Island scattered Hormuz shipping while Iran weighed charging fees for the passage; drone strikes then shut the Saudi line built to bypass Hormuz entirely.

portwatch-taiwan-total.standing: A daily count of merchant vessels passing through the 180-km channel between Taiwan and mainland China, tracked from ship transponder data. It is the main sea lane between Northeast Asian ports and the rest of the world, and the chips Taiwan exports leave through it.
portwatch-taiwan-total.recent: The strait's traffic sits inside a wider squeeze on Asian sea freight: the Houthis took control of Yemen's Red Sea coast, drones shut the Saudi pipeline built to bypass Hormuz, and a projectile that killed a sailor off Qeshm Island pushed Gulf states to shelve their Hormuz talks. With Qatari gas cargoes stalled, China and India burned coal and oil instead, shifting what moves and where.

portwatch-dover-total.standing: The count of vessels moving each day through the Dover Strait, the narrow neck between England and France where North Sea and Atlantic traffic is squeezed into two lanes. It is among the busiest shipping passages anywhere.

portwatch-gibraltar-total.standing: The count of merchant vessels passing daily through the nine-mile-wide channel between Spain and Morocco, the only sea entrance to the Mediterranean. Everything moving between Europe and the Atlantic or Suez crosses it.
portwatch-gibraltar-total.recent: Traffic at the western gate reflected what was happening at the eastern one: a projectile killed a sailor off Qeshm Island and Gulf states shelved the Muscat talks on Hormuz, while Iran weighed charging fees for transit and Houthi fighters took Yemen's port of Mocha. Drone strikes also darkened the Saudi pipeline built to skip Hormuz, leaving the sea route as the only one.

poly-will-united-russia-er-gain-the-most.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether United Russia takes the largest bloc of seats at the next State Duma election. It is a bet on the margin a dominant-party system produces, not on whether the party wins, and traders price the reported result rather than the vote.
poly-will-united-russia-er-gain-the-most.recent: Moscow spent the window escalating rather than negotiating: 863 drones were launched at Ukraine in one night, a drone struck a Warsaw-bound train two kilometers from Poland, strikes on Odesa wounded 37, and Putin called European troops in Ukraine a "war." Against that, US envoys travelled to Russia and Ukraine with a plan to end the fighting.

wiki-israel.standing: The English Wikipedia article on Israel, and how many people open it each day. The count rises when a decision made in or about the country reaches people far outside it, so the line tracks the reach of an event rather than its scale.
wiki-israel.recent: Britain and eleven other states moved to sanction trade from Israeli settlements, and Israel closed the British consulate in Jerusalem that served Palestinians. Haaretz reported the UAE had warned Netanyahu before the October 2023 attack, and he threatened to sue. Washington then approved 40,000 one-ton bombs, taxpayer-funded, on a 15-day congressional clock.

poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether U.S. forces mount a ground invasion of Iran before the start of 2027. It prices how far traders think an air campaign is from becoming an occupation — a distinction oil, shipping and Gulf basing all hang on.
poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.recent: A US government report on Operation Epic Fury put the war's cost above $38 billion and disclosed dozens of aircraft and hundreds of buildings lost, with 18 troops killed; the Pentagon says it has not decided whether damaged Gulf bases will be rebuilt. Its own watchdog found interceptor stocks ran short.

wiki-houthi-movement.standing: The armed movement, formally Ansar Allah, that controls Sanaa and much of northern Yemen. Its reach over the Red Sea coast gives it a hand on one of the world's busiest shipping lanes, so its fighting is felt in freight and oil markets.
wiki-houthi-movement.recent: Fighters took the coffee port of Mokha, then Perim Island, putting the Bab al-Mandab strait under their guns and driving 46,000 people from the Red Sea coast. Missiles hit four Saudi cities and King Khalid Air Base at Khamis Mushait, and drones from Iraq's Maysan province shut the East-West pipeline that lets crude skip Hormuz.

poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.standing: A binary contract on Polymarket that pays out only if the United States has ended its blockade of Iran by the contract's deadline. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, quoted as a percentage, not anyone's forecast.
poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's coverage pointed toward a lifting. Austria revoked Mohammad Eslami's already-granted visa to the Vienna nuclear meeting, Iran's Strait Authority in Tehran widened its non-compliant vessel list to reach tanker insurers, and the Houthis took Yemen's Red Sea coast, stretching the water the US is policing.

wiki-saudi-arabia.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Saudi Arabia, the Gulf kingdom that holds the world's largest spare crude capacity and the shrine cities of Mecca and Medina. Its traffic rises when the country is a party to something.
wiki-saudi-arabia.recent: Ansar Allah fighters seized the Red Sea port of Mocha and islands near Bab el-Mandeb, and on Sept. 8 Houthi missiles hit oil sites in four Saudi cities. Drones launched from Iraq's Maysan province then shut the East-West pipeline, the only line that moves Saudi crude to the sea without passing Hormuz, and Riyadh answered with 54 sorties across five Yemeni provinces.

poly-clarity-act-signed-into-law-in-2026.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether a US crypto market-structure bill called the Clarity Act becomes law before the end of 2026. It prices the odds that Congress finally settles which regulator oversees digital assets.
poly-clarity-act-signed-into-law-in-2026.recent: Republicans rejected the Democrats' counter-proposal on the bill's market-structure language, leaving no path to a floor deal this session and collapsing what traders would pay for passage. The regulatory fight moved to the courts instead: New Jersey asked the Supreme Court to decide whether prediction-market contracts are swaps or gambling, and the UK regulator began weighing an easing of its own ban.

wiki-yemen.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Yemen, the country at the southern end of the Arabian Peninsula. It rises when the war there, or the Bab al-Mandab strait on its coast, forces itself onto the world's front pages.
wiki-yemen.recent: The Houthis took Mokha, the coffee port 75 kilometers from Bab al-Mandab, and with it the Red Sea coast that carries a large share of global shipping; 46,000 people fled that coastline in a week. Saudi jets answered with 54 sorties across five provinces in a day, after Houthi strikes on Saudi energy sites wounded 73.

poly-2026-balance-of-power-d-senate-d-ho.standing: A Polymarket contract that settles in full only if Democrats hold majorities in both chambers of Congress after the 2026 US midterms. Its price is what traders pay for that combined outcome, so both races move it.

poly-fed-rate-hike-in-2026.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if the Federal Reserve raises its policy rate at any point during 2026. It prices the odds of a tightening turn, and mortgage, corporate borrowing and emerging-market currency costs all follow the rate it is betting on.
poly-fed-rate-hike-in-2026.recent: Houthi forces captured Yemen's port of Mocha on 10 September, and the oil price that followed turned an expected cut into an expected hike. Goldman Sachs dropped its no-hike call on 13 September, the 10-year Treasury yield reached 5%, and bond desks built what Bloomberg called an 'extreme' short on the trade.

poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Benjamin Netanyahu will still hold the Israeli premiership after the next change of government. Traders price a coalition's survival, and the outcome shapes Israeli policy on Gaza, Lebanon and the West Bank.
poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.recent: Haaretz reported that the UAE warned Netanyahu of a Hamas plan days before the 2023 attack, and he threatened legal action over it. Against that, Washington approved 40,000 one-ton bombs for Israel, and Bezalel Smotrich moved to void Oslo over Areas A and B, where 2.7 million Palestinians live.

poly-bab-el-mandeb-strait-effectively-cl.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the Bab el-Mandeb strait, the gateway between the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden, will be shut to shipping by a set date. Traders price it as a wager on Yemen's war reaching the sea lane.
poly-bab-el-mandeb-strait-effectively-cl.recent: Houthi forces captured Yemen's Red Sea port of Mocha on Thursday, and oil moved on the news, but traders held the strait itself open: a coastal town changing hands is not a closure, and no shipping ban followed. Separately, New Jersey asked the Supreme Court to rule on whether contracts like this one are swaps or gambling.

poly-fed-rate-hike-by-october-2026-meeti.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the Federal Reserve raises its policy rate at or before the October 2026 meeting. Traders buy and sell the outcome, so the price is what money says is likely, not a forecast.
poly-fed-rate-hike-by-october-2026-meeti.recent: The repricing followed an oil shock: Houthi forces captured Yemen's port of Mocha, pushing crude past $105 and turning the Fed's next move from a cut into a hike. A payroll surge added to it, and Goldman Sachs dropped its no-hike call on Friday as the 10-year Treasury yield reached 5%, its highest since 2007.

stocks:ORCL.standing: Shares in Oracle, a US enterprise software and cloud-infrastructure company listed in New York. It sells databases and business applications, and now rents out the data-centre capacity that AI model training runs on.
stocks:ORCL.recent: Ellison scrapped a planned 50-million-share sale, then filings showed 346 million of his shares pledged as loan collateral worth $50 billion — a stake borrowed against rather than sold. The company is spending an additional $700 million on job cuts to fund AI data centres, with some staff told by an email signed only "Oracle Leadership.

poly-will-the-democratic-party-control-t.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Democrats win a majority of US House seats in the 2026 midterms, settling at 100 or 0 once the results are certified. It is a live price on which party writes the chamber's agenda.
poly-will-the-democratic-party-control-t.recent: The contract barely moved across the window, and nothing in the fortnight's coverage bears on the House race itself — the election news carried far-right gains in Germany's Saxony-Anhalt and a knife-edge Swedish vote, neither of which touches a US midterm. The one directly relevant story was about the venue rather than the bet: New Jersey asked the Supreme Court to decide whether prediction markets are swaps or gambling.

poly-will-gavin-newsom-win-the-2028-demo.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Gavin Newsom wins the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination, with its price read as a percentage. It measures what traders will stake on the California governor, not what any pollster forecasts.

poly-will-china-invade-taiwan-before-202.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if China mounts an armed invasion of Taiwan before the end of 2026. It is the price traders will pay for the single geopolitical break that would cut the semiconductor trade and the sea lanes around it.

poly-will-luiz-incio-lula-da-silva-win-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva wins Brazil's 2026 presidential election. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome — a live market read on whether the incumbent holds the presidency.
poly-will-luiz-incio-lula-da-silva-win-t.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's material accounts for the slide. The single item touching the race is a France 24 report that Flavio Bolsonaro is being probed for corruption as the Brazilian election tightens — a story about trouble on the opposition side, not the incumbent's.

poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if Israel and Iran hold to a ceasefire by a set date. Traders price the odds of the truce surviving, and it is one of the few liquid, continuously updated reads on Middle East escalation risk.
poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.recent: Washington approved a transfer of 40,000 one-ton bombs to Israel, taxpayer-funded, days after the Pentagon's own watchdog said interceptor stocks had run short and a government report put US losses at 18 troops, dozens of aircraft and hundreds of buildings. In Vienna, Austria revoked Mohammad Eslami's visa after granting it, barring Iran's nuclear chief from the IAEA meeting.

poly-us-recession-by-end-of-2026.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the United States enters a recession before the end of 2026, priced as the share traders will pay for a yes. It is a wager on the business cycle, and it reprices whenever growth or rates news lands.
poly-us-recession-by-end-of-2026.recent: The Houthis' capture of Yemen's port of Mocha drove oil sharply higher, arriving on top of a payroll surge and a CPI print that together left traders pricing a September Fed hike near 70%. An oil shock met by tightening rather than easing is the combination this contract is bought against.

poly-will-reza-pahlavi-enter-iran-by-dec.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the exiled son of Iran's last shah sets foot in Iran before the year ends. It is a wager on regime collapse, since no such return is possible while the Islamic Republic controls its borders.
poly-will-reza-pahlavi-enter-iran-by-dec.recent: Six months into the war, the state Pahlavi would return to is damaged but intact: Iran's mission took a General Committee seat in Vienna even after Austria revoked Mohammad Eslami's visa, its air defences downed a $30 million US jet over Isfahan, and UK officials say Tehran still runs cyber operations against exiled critics.

poly-will-jean-luc-mlenchon-win-the-2027.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Jean-Luc Mélenchon, the veteran leader of France's radical left, wins the 2027 presidential election. The price is what traders pay for that outcome, not a poll.

poly-will-gavin-newsom-win-the-2028-us-p.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the California governor wins the 2028 US presidential election. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, in cents on the dollar, years before any ballot is cast.
poly-will-gavin-newsom-win-the-2028-us-p.recent: The fortnight's US political news ran to the machinery of voting rather than the field: New Jersey asked the Supreme Court to decide whether prediction-market contracts are swaps or gambling. That is a question about where this contract may trade, not about who wins, and none of it accounts for the price.

wiki-brics.standing: The intergovernmental grouping built around Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa, now enlarged with further members. It coordinates on trade, development lending and payment arrangements outside Western-led institutions.
wiki-brics.recent: Leaders met in New Delhi and adopted a joint declaration demanding an overhaul of IMF quotas and restating a right of return. Modi ran 15 bilaterals in three days; Putin attended and Iran's Pezeshkian worked the floor mid-war, holding three meetings in one day. Xi pitched an AI "open ecosystem" for the bloc, and India offered its UPI payment rails.

stocks:TEL.OL.standing: Norway's largest telecoms operator, listed in Oslo and majority-owned by the Norwegian state. It runs mobile networks at home and across the Nordics and South and Southeast Asia, which repeatedly puts a government shareholder in charge of commercial decisions abroad.
stocks:TEL.OL.recent: Norway's government opened a probe into the company's Myanmar operations — an awkward arrangement, since the state doing the investigating is also the controlling shareholder in the company being investigated.

poly-iran-charges-hormuz-fees-by-october.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Tehran will begin levying transit charges on ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz by a set date. Roughly a fifth of seaborne oil moves through the strait, so a toll would reprice the whole Gulf export route.
poly-iran-charges-hormuz-fees-by-october.recent: The bet cooled as the leverage behind it moved elsewhere: drones shut the Saudi East-West pipeline, the only line that skips Hormuz, while the Houthis took Yemen's Red Sea coast and the alternate strait with it. Washington's own accounting of Operation Epic Fury — dozens of aircraft, hundreds of buildings, 18 troops dead — left Gulf basing, not tolls, as the open question.

poly-will-flvio-bolsonaro-win-the-2026-b.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Flávio Bolsonaro takes Brazil's presidency in the 2026 election. Traders price the senator son of Jair Bolsonaro as the right's standard-bearer, so the line doubles as a read on how far that coalition can carry the family name.
poly-will-flvio-bolsonaro-win-the-2026-b.recent: France 24 reported on 11 September that Flávio Bolsonaro was under investigation for corruption as the Brazilian race tightened — a probe that has not dented the contract. The fortnight's wider politics ran the same way: the AfD's Saxony-Anhalt landslide and Sweden's far right edging toward government.

poly-will-mohammad-bagher-ghalibaf-atten.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, the speaker of Iran's parliament, appears at a US–Iran summit. It pays on one man showing up in a room, not on any agreement reached there.
poly-will-mohammad-bagher-ghalibaf-atten.recent: Austria revoked a visa it had already granted to Mohammad Eslami, keeping Iran's nuclear chief out of the Vienna meeting even as Iran's mission won a General Committee seat there. Traders were pricing travel to a US-convened table while the US struck new targets in Iran and Tehran promised a 'more painful response'.

stocks:VOD.standing: Shares in the British telecoms group, listed in New York as depositary receipts. It owns mobile networks across Europe and, through its African arm, a payments business that carries a large share of retail transactions in several markets.
stocks:VOD.recent: A court in Nairobi voided an already-completed $1.6 billion sale of a further Safaricom stake to Vodacom, the African arm, and ordered the transaction unwound — a remedy rarely granted once a deal has closed. Vodacom said it will appeal. Safaricom runs M-Pesa, the rail Kenyan households use for wages and school fees.

poly-friedrich-merz-out-as-chancellor-of.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if Friedrich Merz ceases to be Germany's chancellor before the end of 2026. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on coalition strain in Berlin rather than on polling alone.

poly-2026-balance-of-power-r-senate-r-ho.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out only if Republicans hold both the Senate and the House after the 2026 midterm elections. It prices one square of the full outcome grid, so it falls whenever either chamber looks likely to flip.
poly-2026-balance-of-power-r-senate-r-ho.recent: The fortnight's material carried the Clarity Act stalling after Republicans rejected the Democrats' counter-proposal, and a New Jersey petition asking the Supreme Court to rule on prediction markets themselves. Neither bears on who wins either chamber, and nothing here accounts for the price.

stocks:C.standing: The New York-listed shares of Citigroup, one of the four largest US banks and the one most exposed to cross-border business — it moves money for corporations and governments in roughly 90 countries and earns from trade and payment flows.

stocks:META.standing: Shares in the company that owns Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, listed on Nasdaq. Advertising sold against those feeds supplies almost all of its revenue, and it now spends heavily on AI models and headsets built to carry that business somewhere else.
stocks:META.recent: Meta released Muse, a personal AI agent that books travel and sends email on a user's behalf, reachable through WhatsApp — and immediately drew privacy objections over the inbox access that makes it work, plus a scramble after its image tool let anyone build pictures from strangers' Instagram photos. Its chief then rejected calls to slow AI development, arguing liability and outside evaluation suffice.
